hypothesis: Registered SNDK/SPCX shared-portfolio lifecycle contributions can determine whether cash-opening exposure is disproportionately weak under fixed session, accounting and inherited exit-clock conventions.
limitations: All dates and whole-trade results were previously explored; this is descriptive analysis, not an untouched holdout.
Eighteen sensitivity cases reuse 99 noncrypto lifecycles each; source variants are exactly equal for these assets and are not independent samples.
Candle closes have 15-minute resolution and are not native venue mark prices; aligned boundary freshness does not resolve intrabar ordering.
Post-event boundary accounting includes zero-duration fees and a modeled same-timestamp opening exit; raw opening totals differ from selected exposed-date totals.
Paired asset-side dates select opening exposure and retain overlapping lifecycles; their rates do not estimate a causal session penalty.
Whole-lifecycle returns are conserved across clocks; interval differences do not simulate removing trades or preserve counterfactual occupancy.
The original full-fee scenario changes the August 7 modeled SNDK liquidation price as well as fees; no actual venue liquidation is claimed.
Test coverage counts concern two new pure calculation modules, not all I/O, reused engine code or the entire project.
